issues.display_title: Issue #1781: Research: document cancel_users_account.php cancellation/failed-payment flow
issues.main_description_html:
Summary

Research task to document the actual business flow behind cancel_users_account.php (the cron that reacts to failed recurring charges) and produce a gap/strength assessment of the current implementation vs. intended GoThru billing policy.

Current state

  • No documented spec exists for how cancel_users_account.php decides a payment has failed or what it's supposed to do in response.
  • An initial code-only read (not yet validated against actual business intent) found:
    • Three divergent branches — PayPal DirectLink status check, Stripe/Verisign recurring-profile status check, and the manual/queued unsubscribes (unsubscribe_type=1) processor — that each write a different subset of users, user_extra_data, unsubscribes, affiliates_program, and users_cc_renewal_dates.
    • get_stripe_all_trans.php and cc_purchase_complete.php log and then filter out failed charges, but neither feeds into this cron — the cancellation decision is made by re-querying the gateway live, not from logged data.
  • None of this has been confirmed against what GoThru's billing policy is actually supposed to be.

Target state

A short written doc (place under the repo's existing spec/notes convention — see the pattern used for #1778) that answers:

  1. What is GoThru's intended policy on a failed recurring charge — grace period, immediate downgrade, dunning emails, retry count? (Get this from whoever owns billing, not just from the code.)
  2. Does the current code match that policy, per gateway (Stripe subscription, Stripe customer, PayPal DirectLink, Verisign recurring profile)?
  3. Concrete gap list, each confirmed intentional or bug, e.g.: affiliates_program.pay_active and users_cc_renewal_dates.subscribed are only updated on user-initiated cancel (unsubscribe_type=1), never on auto-cancel from a failed charge (unsubscribe_type=2).
  4. Concrete strengths worth preserving, e.g. the unsubscribes pending-request guard in the RP/Stripe branch that stops a user mid-grace-period from being double-cancelled.
  5. Confirm or dismiss two defects found in the initial read: the dead condition at get_stripe_all_trans.php:89 (checks $val['respmsg'], but the key actually set is respm, so the branch never fires), and the live Stripe secret key hardcoded in plaintext, duplicated across get_stripe_all_trans.php, cc_purchase_complete.php, and cancel_users_account.php.

Scope

  • gothru.co/cancel_users_account.php
  • gothru.co/get_stripe_all_trans.php
  • gothru.co/cc_purchase_complete.php
  • Tables: users, user_extra_data, unsubscribes, affiliates_program, users_cc_renewal_dates, cc_logs, cc_logs_stripe, cc_purchase
  • Confirm intended behavior with whoever owns billing/subscription business rules.

Out of scope

  • No code changes in this task — research and documentation only. File separate implementation issues once gaps are confirmed as real bugs to fix.

Risk / test plan

N/A — research task. Deliverable is a written doc, reviewed and confirmed against actual GoThru billing policy rather than tested as code.

Result

Full write-up: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-14-cancel-users-account-cron-research.md

  • 6 independent branches in cancel_users_account.php, no single cancellation path — trigger + writes mapped for each.
  • Both suspected defects confirmed: dead respmsg condition at get_stripe_all_trans.php:89, and the hardcoded live Stripe key (4x in this file's immediate family, 40+ across gothru.co overall).
  • Live Stripe data pulled with a new read-only tool (php artisan payment:check-stripe-dunning) confirms the real grace window: 21-day/5-attempt dunning, then a further ~9-10 days until Stripe auto-cancels, then up to 1 day cron lag — 3+ weeks minimum, no cap, and the user keeps full paid access the entire time.
  • 10 confirmed gaps total, including zero customer email during the whole dunning window, an email-subject leak between branches, overlay-deactivation code that's commented out while the email still claims it ran, and a PayPal-legacy manual-cancel path that skips the confirmation email entirely.
  • Billing-policy questions (grace period acceptability, downgrade-vs-hard-cancel intent, per-gateway policy) are still open, flagged for the billing owner in the doc.

No code changes made — per scope, will file separate implementation issues once gaps are confirmed as real bugs to fix.
